packs.title: OOP interview
packs.blurb: Common OOP interview questions (SOLID, patterns, design smells).

questions.text: What does the Single Responsibility Principle say?
hints: Do not mix I/O and rules.
questions.rubric: A class should have one reason to change — one job. Mixing persistence, HTTP, and business rules in one type makes every change risky. Split those axes so a schema change does not touch your HTTP layer.
questions.answer: A class should have one reason to change — one job. Mixing persistence, HTTP, and business rules in one type makes every change risky. Split those axes so a schema change does not touch your HTTP layer.

questions.text: What does the Open/Closed Principle say?
questions.rubric: Open for extension, closed for modification. Add behavior via new types or composition (strategy, plugins) instead of editing a switch every time a variant appears. Inheritance is one tool, not the only one.
questions.answer: Open for extension, closed for modification. Add behavior via new types or composition (strategy, plugins) instead of editing a switch every time a variant appears. Inheritance is one tool, not the only one.

questions.text: What is the Liskov Substitution Principle?
questions.rubric: A subtype must be usable wherever the base type is expected without breaking callers. Throwing in an override, narrowing outputs, or strengthening preconditions violates it. Square/rectangle is the classic trap.
questions.answer: A subtype must be usable wherever the base type is expected without breaking callers. Throwing in an override, narrowing outputs, or strengthening preconditions violates it. Square/rectangle is the classic trap.

questions.text: What is the Interface Segregation Principle?
questions.rubric: Prefer many small interfaces over one fat one. Callers should not depend on methods they never use. A Worker that must implement eat() because of a God interface is the smell.
questions.answer: Prefer many small interfaces over one fat one. Callers should not depend on methods they never use. A Worker that must implement eat() because of a God interface is the smell.

questions.text: What is the Dependency Inversion Principle?
questions.rubric: High-level policy should depend on abstractions, not on concrete I/O. Inject a Port/interface; the adapter (SQL, HTTP) implements it. That is DIP, not merely "use a DI container."
questions.answer: High-level policy should depend on abstractions, not on concrete I/O. Inject a Port/interface; the adapter (SQL, HTTP) implements it. That is DIP, not merely "use a DI container."

questions.rubric: Hide representation behind a small public API. Invariants live in constructors and mutators. Getters for every field is not encapsulation — it leaks the model.
questions.answer: Hide representation behind a small public API. Invariants live in constructors and mutators. Getters for every field is not encapsulation — it leaks the model.

questions.rubric: Show the essential operations, hide the rest. An interface or abstract type names the capability (Payable, Repository). Abstraction is about the vocabulary, not about drawing UML.
questions.answer: Show the essential operations, hide the rest. An interface or abstract type names the capability (Payable, Repository). Abstraction is about the vocabulary, not about drawing UML.

questions.rubric: The same message, different behavior. Subtype polymorphism (override), parametric (generics), and ad-hoc (overloads). Interviews usually want subtype: a list of Shapes each draws itself.
questions.answer: The same message, different behavior. Subtype polymorphism (override), parametric (generics), and ad-hoc (overloads). Interviews usually want subtype: a list of Shapes each draws itself.

questions.text: When do you prefer composition over inheritance?
questions.rubric: When you need behavior reuse without an is-a relationship. Inheritance couples lifecycles and breaks LSP easily. Compose a Logger or Strategy instead of subclassing for every variant.
questions.answer: When you need behavior reuse without an is-a relationship. Inheritance couples lifecycles and breaks LSP easily. Compose a Logger or Strategy instead of subclassing for every variant.

questions.text: What is the difference between is-a and has-a?
questions.rubric: is-a is inheritance/subtyping (Dog is an Animal). has-a is composition (Car has an Engine). Model has-a with fields; force is-a only when substitution holds.
questions.answer: is-a is inheritance/subtyping (Dog is an Animal). has-a is composition (Car has an Engine). Model has-a with fields; force is-a only when substitution holds.

questions.rubric: How strongly a type's methods belong together. High cohesion: one topic. Low cohesion: a Utils dumping ground. High cohesion makes SRP easier.
questions.answer: How strongly a type's methods belong together. High cohesion: one topic. Low cohesion: a Utils dumping ground. High cohesion makes SRP easier.

questions.rubric: How much one module knows about another. Tight coupling: concrete classes, shared mutable state. Loose: interfaces, messages, immutability. You want high cohesion, low coupling.
questions.answer: How much one module knows about another. Tight coupling: concrete classes, shared mutable state. Loose: interfaces, messages, immutability. You want high cohesion, low coupling.

questions.rubric: Both are has-a. Composition: part dies with the whole (Order owns LineItems). Aggregation: parts can outlive the whole (Department has Employees). In code both are fields; the distinction is lifetime.
questions.answer: Both are has-a. Composition: part dies with the whole (Order owns LineItems). Aggregation: parts can outlive the whole (Department has Employees). In code both are fields; the distinction is lifetime.

questions.rubric: A relationship between objects that is not ownership — a Teacher associated with Courses. In code: a reference or a join table. Weaker than composition.
questions.answer: A relationship between objects that is not ownership — a Teacher associated with Courses. In code: a reference or a join table. Weaker than composition.

questions.rubric: Establish a valid object. Fail fast if invariants cannot hold. Avoid real I/O in constructors — inject collaborators already built. Overloaded constructors should funnel to one.
questions.answer: Establish a valid object. Fail fast if invariants cannot hold. Avoid real I/O in constructors — inject collaborators already built. Overloaded constructors should funnel to one.

questions.text: What is a destructor or finalizer for?
questions.rubric: Release native resources. In GC languages prefer AutoCloseable/with/using; finalizers are late and unreliable. C++ RAII ties lifetime to stack unwind.
questions.answer: Release native resources. In GC languages prefer AutoCloseable/with/using; finalizers are late and unreliable. C++ RAII ties lifetime to stack unwind.

questions.text: What are public, private, and protected for?
questions.rubric: Public is the API. Private is representation. Protected is for subclasses — easy to overuse and leak internals. Default/package is a fourth mode in Java.
questions.answer: Public is the API. Private is representation. Protected is for subclasses — easy to overuse and leak internals. Default/package is a fourth mode in Java.

questions.rubric: Overload: same name, different parameters, chosen at compile time. Override: same signature in a subclass, chosen at runtime (virtual dispatch). Hiding static methods is neither.
questions.answer: Overload: same name, different parameters, chosen at compile time. Override: same signature in a subclass, chosen at runtime (virtual dispatch). Hiding static methods is neither.

questions.text: When is an abstract class better than an interface?
questions.rubric: When you have shared fields or implemented methods to reuse. Interfaces (or Protocols) when you only need a capability. Languages with default interface methods blur this.
questions.answer: When you have shared fields or implemented methods to reuse. Interfaces (or Protocols) when you only need a capability. Languages with default interface methods blur this.

questions.text: Why do many languages restrict multiple inheritance?
questions.rubric: State and diamonds. Interfaces/traits/mixins give behavior reuse without two full class layouts. If you need MI, keep mixins tiny and stateless.
questions.answer: State and diamonds. Interfaces/traits/mixins give behavior reuse without two full class layouts. If you need MI, keep mixins tiny and stateless.

questions.text: Why are immutable objects easier to reason about?
questions.rubric: No aliasing bugs, safe sharing across threads, good map keys. Cost: more allocations. Records/data classes with frozen=true encode this.
questions.answer: No aliasing bugs, safe sharing across threads, good map keys. Cost: more allocations. Records/data classes with frozen=true encode this.

questions.rubric: Tell an object to do work instead of pulling its data and deciding outside. Ask-style getters + external ifs is feature envy. Command methods keep invariants inside.
questions.answer: Tell an object to do work instead of pulling its data and deciding outside. Ask-style getters + external ifs is feature envy. Command methods keep invariants inside.

questions.text: What is the Law of Demeter?
questions.rubric: Talk only to your immediate friends: a.b() not a.getB().getC().foo(). Long chains couple you to a graph. Fix with a method on the neighbor that does the job.
questions.answer: Talk only to your immediate friends: a.b() not a.getB().getC().foo(). Long chains couple you to a graph. Fix with a method on the neighbor that does the job.

questions.rubric: Parnas: hide design decisions likely to change. Encapsulation is the OOP mechanism. A stable interface with a replaceable guts is the point of modules.
questions.answer: Parnas: hide design decisions likely to change. Encapsulation is the OOP mechanism. A stable interface with a replaceable guts is the point of modules.

questions.rubric: When two similar blocks will diverge. Premature abstraction couples unrelated change. Duplicate until you know the third copy's shape, then extract.
questions.answer: When two similar blocks will diverge. Premature abstraction couples unrelated change. Duplicate until you know the third copy's shape, then extract.

hints: Do not build unused extension points.
questions.rubric: You aren't gonna need it. Do not build the plugin system for one customer. Complexity now has a carrying cost. Revisit when the second use appears.
questions.answer: You aren't gonna need it. Do not build the plugin system for one customer. Complexity now has a carrying cost. Revisit when the second use appears.

questions.rubric: Keep the design as simple as the problem. No framework for a script. Simple code is easier to prove and to delete.
questions.answer: Keep the design as simple as the problem. No framework for a script. Simple code is easier to prove and to delete.

questions.rubric: One type that knows everything and does everything. Symptoms: thousands of lines, every change touches it. Split along responsibilities (SRP) and hide data.
questions.answer: One type that knows everything and does everything. Symptoms: thousands of lines, every change touches it. Split along responsibilities (SRP) and hide data.

questions.rubric: A method that uses another type's data more than its own. The method probably belongs on that other type. Move it.
questions.answer: A method that uses another type's data more than its own. The method probably belongs on that other type. Move it.

questions.rubric: One change ripples across many files. The opposite of SRP at the change-set level. Re-bundle the scattered bits into one module.
questions.answer: One change ripples across many files. The opposite of SRP at the change-set level. Re-bundle the scattered bits into one module.

questions.text: What is an anemic domain model?
questions.rubric: Entities are bags of getters; all rules live in services. Easy to persist, weak encapsulation. A rich model puts invariants on the entity; services orchestrate.
questions.answer: Entities are bags of getters; all rules live in services. Easy to persist, weak encapsulation. A rich model puts invariants on the entity; services orchestrate.

questions.text: What is the difference between a DTO and an entity?
questions.rubric: A DTO is a boundary payload — no invariants, serializable. An entity has identity and rules. Do not send entities over the wire; map at the edge.
questions.answer: A DTO is a boundary payload — no invariants, serializable. An entity has identity and rules. Do not send entities over the wire; map at the edge.

questions.rubric: Equality by value, no identity (Money, Email). Immutable. Two Money(5, USD) are the same. Entities have identity even if fields match.
questions.answer: Equality by value, no identity (Money, Email). Immutable. Two Money(5, USD) are the same. Entities have identity even if fields match.

questions.text: What is identity for an entity?
questions.rubric: A stable id independent of attributes. A User renamed is still that User. Databases use primary keys; in memory use an id field, not object identity.
questions.answer: A stable id independent of attributes. A User renamed is still that User. Databases use primary keys; in memory use an id field, not object identity.

questions.rubric: Pass collaborators in (constructor preferred) instead of new-ing them inside. Enables tests and DIP. A container is optional; poor-man's DI is still DI.
questions.answer: Pass collaborators in (constructor preferred) instead of new-ing them inside. Enables tests and DIP. A container is optional; poor-man's DI is still DI.

questions.text: When do you use a factory?
questions.rubric: When creation is non-trivial or you want to return a subtype without the caller naming it. Factory method vs abstract factory: one method vs a family of products.
questions.answer: When creation is non-trivial or you want to return a subtype without the caller naming it. Factory method vs abstract factory: one method vs a family of products.

questions.text: Why is Singleton often a smell?
questions.rubric: Hidden global state, hard tests, hidden coupling, and threading bugs. Prefer injecting a single instance from composition root. Use it only for true process-wide resources with care.
questions.answer: Hidden global state, hard tests, hidden coupling, and threading bugs. Prefer injecting a single instance from composition root. Use it only for true process-wide resources with care.

questions.rubric: A family of algorithms behind one interface, selected at runtime. Replaces if/else on type. Pairs with DIP: inject the strategy.
questions.answer: A family of algorithms behind one interface, selected at runtime. Replaces if/else on type. Pairs with DIP: inject the strategy.

questions.rubric: Publishers notify subscribers of events without knowing who they are. UI, metrics, domain events. Watch leaks: unsubscribe. For process-wide, prefer a message bus.
questions.answer: Publishers notify subscribers of events without knowing who they are. UI, metrics, domain events. Watch leaks: unsubscribe. For process-wide, prefer a message bus.

questions.rubric: Wrap an object with the same interface to add behavior (logging, retry, cache). Composition of wrappers. Different from Python @decorator syntax, same idea.
questions.answer: Wrap an object with the same interface to add behavior (logging, retry, cache). Composition of wrappers. Different from Python @decorator syntax, same idea.

questions.rubric: Make an existing type satisfy a target interface without changing it. Wrap the foreign API. Used at system boundaries.
questions.answer: Make an existing type satisfy a target interface without changing it. Wrap the foreign API. Used at system boundaries.

hints: Not a God class if thin.
questions.rubric: A simple front for a messy subsystem. Not a God object if it only forwards. Use it so callers do not know three SDKs.
questions.answer: A simple front for a messy subsystem. Not a God object if it only forwards. Use it so callers do not know three SDKs.

questions.rubric: Both wrap. Proxy controls access (lazy, remote, auth). Decorator adds responsibilities. Same structure, different intent.
questions.answer: Both wrap. Proxy controls access (lazy, remote, auth). Decorator adds responsibilities. Same structure, different intent.

questions.rubric: Many optional parameters, or a multi-step immutable build. Telescoping constructors do not scale. In Python, dataclasses with defaults often beat a builder.
questions.answer: Many optional parameters, or a multi-step immutable build. Telescoping constructors do not scale. In Python, dataclasses with defaults often beat a builder.

questions.rubric: A base class defines the algorithm skeleton; subclasses fill steps. Rigid — prefer Strategy or functions when the language has first-class functions.
questions.answer: A base class defines the algorithm skeleton; subclasses fill steps. Rigid — prefer Strategy or functions when the language has first-class functions.

questions.rubric: An object that represents a request: execute/undo, queue, log. Useful for undo stacks and job queues. Do not invent it for a single function call.
questions.answer: An object that represents a request: execute/undo, queue, log. Useful for undo stacks and job queues. Do not invent it for a single function call.

questions.rubric: Replace a status enum + giant switch with objects per state, each knowing the transitions. Good when transition rules are rich.
questions.answer: Replace a status enum + giant switch with objects per state, each knowing the transitions. Good when transition rules are rich.

questions.rubric: Handlers in a line; each can handle or pass on. Middleware and servlet filters. Order matters; always have a terminal handler.
questions.answer: Handlers in a line; each can handle or pass on. Middleware and servlet filters. Order matters; always have a terminal handler.

questions.rubric: Treat a tree of objects uniformly: File and Directory both implement Node. Recursion on children. UI view trees and AST nodes.
questions.answer: Treat a tree of objects uniformly: File and Directory both implement Node. Recursion on children. UI view trees and AST nodes.

questions.rubric: Share immutable intrinsic state across many objects (characters in an editor, RGB). Extrinsic state is passed in. A cache of interned values.
questions.answer: Share immutable intrinsic state across many objects (characters in an editor, RGB). Extrinsic state is passed in. A cache of interned values.

questions.text: What is Iterator as a pattern?
questions.rubric: Sequential access without exposing representation. In Python, __iter__/__next__. Do not mutate the collection while iterating unless the iterator documents it.
questions.answer: Sequential access without exposing representation. In Python, __iter__/__next__. Do not mutate the collection while iterating unless the iterator documents it.

questions.rubric: An implementation that does nothing instead of null. Avoids null checks. Do not use it to hide missing required collaborators.
questions.answer: An implementation that does nothing instead of null. Avoids null checks. Do not use it to hide missing required collaborators.

questions.text: What is hexagonal / ports and adapters?
questions.rubric: Domain in the middle; ports are interfaces; adapters talk HTTP/SQL. Tests hit ports. Same as onion/clean at this zoom. DIP at architecture scale.
questions.answer: Domain in the middle; ports are interfaces; adapters talk HTTP/SQL. Tests hit ports. Same as onion/clean at this zoom. DIP at architecture scale.

questions.text: What is Clean Architecture's dependency rule?
questions.rubric: Dependencies point inward: frameworks depend on use cases, not the reverse. Entities do not import HTTP. Outer layers implement inner interfaces.
questions.answer: Dependencies point inward: frameworks depend on use cases, not the reverse. Entities do not import HTTP. Outer layers implement inner interfaces.

questions.text: Why package by feature instead of by layer?
questions.rubric: A feature folder has its UI, domain, and persistence together, so a change stays local. Layer packages (all controllers together) make every feature a shotgun surgery.
questions.answer: A feature folder has its UI, domain, and persistence together, so a change stays local. Layer packages (all controllers together) make every feature a shotgun surgery.

hints: Not the same as event sourcing.
questions.rubric: Separate read models from write models. Writes keep invariants; reads can be denormalized. Not event sourcing — you can CQRS a single database with two queries.
questions.answer: Separate read models from write models. Writes keep invariants; reads can be denormalized. Not event sourcing — you can CQRS a single database with two queries.

questions.rubric: Store facts (events), rebuild state by folding. Audit for free; reads need projections. Operationally harder. Do not start there without a reason.
questions.answer: Store facts (events), rebuild state by folding. Audit for free; reads need projections. Operationally harder. Do not start there without a reason.

questions.rubric: A DDD boundary where a word has one meaning. User in Billing is not User in Identity. Map at the edges. Stops one giant model.
questions.answer: A DDD boundary where a word has one meaning. User in Billing is not User in Identity. Map at the edges. Stops one giant model.

questions.rubric: A cluster of entities with a root and a consistency boundary. Change through the root. One transaction per aggregate. References to others by id.
questions.answer: A cluster of entities with a root and a consistency boundary. Change through the root. One transaction per aggregate. References to others by id.

questions.rubric: In constructors and mutating methods of the type that owns them, or in a domain service if they span aggregates. Not in the UI. Fail fast.
questions.answer: In constructors and mutating methods of the type that owns them, or in a domain service if they span aggregates. Not in the UI. Fail fast.

questions.text: Why are bidirectional object graphs painful?
questions.rubric: JSON cycles, equality recursion, and unclear ownership. Prefer one direction. If you need both, pick an owner and keep the back-pointer derived.
questions.answer: JSON cycles, equality recursion, and unclear ownership. Prefer one direction. If you need both, pick an owner and keep the back-pointer derived.

questions.rubric: Equal objects must have equal hashes; hash must be stable while the object is in a HashMap. Mutable keys are a bug. LSP: subclasses must not break equals symmetry.
questions.answer: Equal objects must have equal hashes; hash must be stable while the object is in a HashMap. Mutable keys are a bug. LSP: subclasses must not break equals symmetry.

questions.rubric: Shallow vs deep, final fields, and identity. Prefer an explicit copy constructor or factory. In Python, copy vs deepcopy is the same conversation.
questions.answer: Shallow vs deep, final fields, and identity. Prefer an explicit copy constructor or factory. In Python, copy vs deepcopy is the same conversation.

questions.text: What is the OOP risk with serialization?
questions.rubric: It bypasses constructors, so invariants can break. Versioning fields is hard. Prefer explicit mappers to DTOs over dumping the domain graph.
questions.answer: It bypasses constructors, so invariants can break. Versioning fields is hard. Prefer explicit mappers to DTOs over dumping the domain graph.

questions.rubric: A closed hierarchy the compiler knows. Exhaustive switches, no surprise subclasses. Java sealed, Kotlin sealed, Scala. Algebraic data types in OOP clothing.
questions.answer: A closed hierarchy the compiler knows. Exhaustive switches, no surprise subclasses. Java sealed, Kotlin sealed, Scala. Algebraic data types in OOP clothing.

questions.text: When do you make a class final?
questions.rubric: When it is not designed for inheritance (Effective Java). Inheritance is a contract. Default to final/closed; open only types you document as extensible.
questions.answer: When it is not designed for inheritance (Effective Java). Inheritance is a contract. Default to final/closed; open only types you document as extensible.

questions.rubric: A class meant to be composed into others to provide methods, often without being instantiated. Python mixins, Scala traits. Keep them stateless to avoid diamonds.
questions.answer: A class meant to be composed into others to provide methods, often without being instantiated. Python mixins, Scala traits. Keep them stateless to avoid diamonds.

questions.rubric: Covariant: a Producer<Cat> is a Producer<Animal> (outputs). Contravariant: a Consumer<Animal> is a Consumer<Cat> (inputs). Java PECS: producer extends, consumer super.
questions.answer: Covariant: a Producer<Cat> is a Producer<Animal> (outputs). Contravariant: a Consumer<Animal> is a Consumer<Cat> (inputs). Java PECS: producer extends, consumer super.

questions.text: What is type erasure in Java generics?
questions.rubric: Type parameters are not available at runtime. You cannot new T() or inspect T without a Class token. Arrays of T are awkward. Kotlin/Scala have reified in limited cases.
questions.answer: Type parameters are not available at runtime. You cannot new T() or inspect T without a Class token. Arrays of T are awkward. Kotlin/Scala have reified in limited cases.

questions.text: What is the difference between a class and an object?
questions.rubric: A class is the definition (blueprint). An object is an instance with identity and state. In Python, classes are objects too (instances of type).
questions.answer: A class is the definition (blueprint). An object is an instance with identity and state. In Python, classes are objects too (instances of type).

questions.text: What does "sending a message" mean in OOP?
questions.rubric: Smalltalk: you send a message, the object decides the method. In Java/Python that is a method call with dynamic dispatch. The point is the receiver chooses.
questions.answer: Smalltalk: you send a message, the object decides the method. In Java/Python that is a method call with dynamic dispatch. The point is the receiver chooses.

questions.text: How does OOP differ from procedural programming?
questions.rubric: Procedural: functions + data structures. OOP: data and the operations that preserve its invariants live together, with polymorphism for variants. Both can be abused.
questions.answer: Procedural: functions + data structures. OOP: data and the operations that preserve its invariants live together, with polymorphism for variants. Both can be abused.

questions.text: When is functional style a better fit than OOP?
questions.rubric: Transformations over immutable data, no identity, easy parallelism. OOP fits long-lived identity and invariants. Real systems mix: immutable values inside services.
questions.answer: Transformations over immutable data, no identity, easy parallelism. OOP fits long-lived identity and invariants. Real systems mix: immutable values inside services.

questions.text: Does SRP apply only to classes?
questions.rubric: No — functions, modules, and services too. A deployable with five reasons to ship is the same smell. Name the axis of change.
questions.answer: No — functions, modules, and services too. A deployable with five reasons to ship is the same smell. Name the axis of change.

questions.text: How do you apply Open/Closed without inheritance?
questions.rubric: Callbacks, registries, Strategy objects, config-driven handlers. A map of type → function is OCP. Inheritance is optional.
questions.answer: Callbacks, registries, Strategy objects, config-driven handlers. A map of type → function is OCP. Inheritance is optional.

questions.text: Why is throwing UnsupportedOperationException in an override an LSP risk?
hints: Do not lie in the subtype.
questions.rubric: Callers of the base type do not expect that. You cannot substitute the subtype. Split interfaces (ISP) instead of a wide base that some children cannot honor.
questions.answer: Callers of the base type do not expect that. You cannot substitute the subtype. Split interfaces (ISP) instead of a wide base that some children cannot honor.

questions.text: What is a classic Interface Segregation example with a printer?
questions.rubric: Do not force a Scanner on a simple Printer. Printable vs Scannable vs Faxable. Clients depend on the slice they need.
questions.answer: Do not force a Scanner on a simple Printer. Printable vs Scannable vs Faxable. Clients depend on the slice they need.

hints: No SQL in the use case.
questions.rubric: You inject a fake Port. The use case never imports SQL. Tests do not boot a database. That is the test seam.
questions.answer: You inject a fake Port. The use case never imports SQL. Tests do not boot a database. That is the test seam.

questions.rubric: The one place (main, a framework bootstrap) that new-s concrete types and wires the graph. The rest of the app receives interfaces. Avoid service-locator calls deep in the tree.
questions.answer: The one place (main, a framework bootstrap) that new-s concrete types and wires the graph. The rest of the app receives interfaces. Avoid service-locator calls deep in the tree.

questions.text: Why is a service locator a smell next to DI?
questions.rubric: It hides dependencies: you cannot see what a class needs from its constructor. Tests must set up a global. Prefer constructor injection.
questions.answer: It hides dependencies: you cannot see what a class needs from its constructor. Tests must set up a global. Prefer constructor injection.

questions.text: What is a fluent interface risk?
questions.rubric: Readability vs debugging and partial builds. A builder that can be left invalid is a footgun. Make build() validate.
questions.answer: Readability vs debugging and partial builds. A builder that can be left invalid is a footgun. Make build() validate.

questions.rubric: An empty interface used as a tag (Serializable). Fragile versus an annotation/attribute. Prefer explicit capabilities.
questions.answer: An empty interface used as a tag (Serializable). Fragile versus an annotation/attribute. Prefer explicit capabilities.

questions.text: What runtime cost do objects have?
questions.rubric: Headers, alignment, virtual tables, pointer chasing. Lots of tiny objects hurt caches. Value types/records/structs reduce that where the language allows.
questions.answer: Headers, alignment, virtual tables, pointer chasing. Lots of tiny objects hurt caches. Value types/records/structs reduce that where the language allows.

questions.text: What lives on the stack versus the heap in typical OOP runtimes?
questions.rubric: Locals and return addresses on the stack; objects on the heap (Java/Python/C#). C++ can put objects on the stack. Escape analysis can stack-allocate in JVMs.
questions.answer: Locals and return addresses on the stack; objects on the heap (Java/Python/C#). C++ can put objects on the stack. Escape analysis can stack-allocate in JVMs.

questions.text: How does GC compare to RAII for resources?
questions.rubric: GC reclaims memory, not files/sockets, in time. RAII/with/using is deterministic for those. Use both: GC for memory, context managers for I/O.
questions.answer: GC reclaims memory, not files/sockets, in time. RAII/with/using is deterministic for those. Use both: GC for memory, context managers for I/O.

questions.rubric: A method calling another method on this uses the runtime type, so a base-class method can hit a subclass override. Powerful and surprising. Document it or avoid it in constructors.
questions.answer: A method calling another method on this uses the runtime type, so a base-class method can hit a subclass override. Powerful and surprising. Document it or avoid it in constructors.

questions.text: What is the fragile base class problem?
questions.rubric: A change in a parent silently breaks subclasses that overrode assumptions. Prefer composition; keep inheritance trees shallow and documented.
questions.answer: A change in a parent silently breaks subclasses that overrode assumptions. Prefer composition; keep inheritance trees shallow and documented.

questions.text: What is yo-yo problem in inheritance?
questions.rubric: Reading a method means bouncing up and down a deep hierarchy. Flatten or compose. A sign the tree is too deep.
questions.answer: Reading a method means bouncing up and down a deep hierarchy. Flatten or compose. A sign the tree is too deep.

questions.rubric: A subclass inherits methods it does not want and disables them. LSP/ISP failure. Split the parent.
questions.answer: A subclass inherits methods it does not want and disables them. LSP/ISP failure. Split the parent.

questions.rubric: The same three fields travel together through many signatures. They want to be a type (Address, DateRange). Extract a value object.
questions.answer: The same three fields travel together through many signatures. They want to be a type (Address, DateRange). Extract a value object.

questions.rubric: Using raw strings/ints for Email, Money, UserId. No validation. Wrap in value objects.
questions.answer: Using raw strings/ints for Email, Money, UserId. No validation. Wrap in value objects.

questions.text: Why is a switch on type a polymorphism smell?
questions.rubric: Every new variant edits the switch (OCP). Prefer a method on the type or a visitor if you have many operations over a closed set.
questions.answer: Every new variant edits the switch (OCP). Prefer a method on the type or a visitor if you have many operations over a closed set.

questions.rubric: Many operations over a stable closed hierarchy (compilers, ASTs). Double dispatch. Overkill if the set of types grows more than operations.
questions.answer: Many operations over a stable closed hierarchy (compilers, ASTs). Double dispatch. Overkill if the set of types grows more than operations.

questions.rubric: A snapshot of state for undo without exposing guts. Heavy. Undo stacks often store commands instead.
